cubes.text: The living room is quiet except for the low murmur of the television. Your {{dad}} lowers himself onto the couch beside you with a familiar grunt.
What the hell is this crap you're watching?
I don't even know. I was bored, so I turned the TV on.
Bored? You kids don't know boredom. When I was your age, only two channels, and let me tell ya, they showed dust and test patterns half the time, hahaha.
Here it comes. -The when I was a boy- saga.
I won't punish you with all that. But I'll say this: bad TV was the best thing that happened to me. It pushed me outside, where I could meet girls and actually have fun.
{{dad}} , I already know about the birds and the bees. No need for the talk.
Relax, I'm not launching into the talk. I'm just saying the world's more interesting than that glowing box. That's all. Just advice.
The two of you sit in comfortable silence for a beat, the TV still mumbling to itself. Then your father grins, the kind of grin that always comes before something incredibly stupid.
You know, back in my day, we didn't have remote controls. But I never needed batteries to turn a woman on.
He winks, then pats your knee like he just delivered the punchline of the century.
